name: Uriah
whenBasis: In David's reign, ≈1010–970 BC, counted back from Solomon as Thiele does.
summary: A Hittite, one of David's mighty men, married to Bathsheba. While he was at the siege of Rabbah, David slept with his wife. Called home to cover it, he would not go down to his house while the ark and the army were in tents; so David sent him back with a letter to Joab to put him in the fiercest fighting, and he was killed.
body: Twice he sleeps at the palace door. “As surely as you live,” he tells David, “I will not do such a thing.” David gets him drunk and still he does not go home. He carries his own death warrant to Joab.
Nathan's parable of the rich man who took the poor man's one ewe lamb is about him. Matthew's genealogy names Solomon's mother as “the wife of Uriah.”

media.caption: David gives Uriah a letter for Joab (2 Samuel 11:14), Pieter Lastman, 1619. The Leiden Collection.
